newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TYPHOON TINA HALTS SOUTH KOREAN BUNKER OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: TYPHOON TINA HALTS SOUTH KOREAN BUNKER OPERATIONS.

text.p: South Korean oil companies have stopped bunker operations as typhoon Tina approached the country's coast, industry sources said on Friday.
Some oil refineries on the southern end of the Korean peninsular such as Yukong Ltd and LG-Caltex Oil Corp have closed their terminals.
"The Ulsan port authority has ordered every ship at the anchorage to take shelter at other inland ports," one bunker source said.
The sources said both Yukong and LG-Caltex closed their terminals early on Friday and were only expected to re-open late Saturday or early Sunday when typhoon Tina is expected to pass.
However, their refineries were operating normally despite the shutdown of the terminal, the sources said.
Yukong is South Korea's largest refiner with a 810,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) capacity in Ulsan. LG-Caltex is the second biggest with a 600,000-bpd capacity.
One bunker source said the other bunker terminals in Yeochon and Pusan had also closed.

Industry sources said the closure of the South Korean ports for at least two days would mean a boom for operators in Singapore, as ships orginally planning to refuel in South Korea would now do so in Singapore.
"The two-day closure might lead to some berth congestion or delays and shipowners might just avoid South Korea and take their bunker in Singapore to save time," one bunker supplier in Singapore said.
South Korea has Asia's second largest bunker industry, supplying just under 10 million tonnes a year. Singapore, the largest bunker port in Asia, supplied 16.9 million tonnes in 1996.
